newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Top Russian paratrooper sacked after backing Lebed.
newsitem.headline: Top Russian paratrooper sacked after backing Lebed.

text.p: The deputy commander of Russia's airborne troops, Vladimir Kazantsev, was sacked on Thursday after opposing a decision by Defence Minister Igor Rodionov to reorganise and cut his force.
A spokesman for the airborne troops said the decision had been taken by top defence ministry generals.
He gave no details but a source in the force said Kazantsev had been accused of "discrediting the leadership of the defence ministry" and "violating ethical norms".
Russia's security chief Alexander Lebed, a reserve paratroop general, on Tuesday backed the paratroop command in opposing Rodionov's decision to reorganise the force, calling his order "criminal".
Kazantsev called a news conference on Wednesday to oppose Rodionov's move and back Lebed.
Rodionov defended his decision on Wednesday, saying it was a neccessary part of his military reform. He said Lebed's criticism was motivated by the fact he used to be a paratrooper.
Lebed is also locked in a bitter row with Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov who accused him of trying to seize power while President Boris Yeltsin is preparing for a heart operation.
